summary.name: Postman
summary.one_liner: Postman is an API development platform that now offers a CLI and pre-built agent skills for running collections, tests, and API workflows from a coding agent.
use_cases: Run API collections and tests from a coding agent
Generate request collections and assertions to catch regressions
Mock an API before the backend exists
Monitor live endpoints for uptime and drift
Run collection and governance checks on every commit
Let agents call APIs without holding secrets
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a Postman CLI that installs into a coding agent via the command "postman init", which loads Postman's agent skills to run collections, tests, and API workflows. A marketplace lists skills for API discovery, testing, mocking, monitoring, CI integration, and performance testing. The Context Graph is described as a structured, queryable map of an organization's APIs, collections, and relationships for grounding agent-generated calls and tests. Passport is described as a way for people, services, and agents to call APIs without holding the secret, with a proxy that validates the caller and scope, and logs each request against the caller's identity.
notable: Postman CLI with pre-built agent skills installable into coding agents such as Claude
Context Graph maps APIs, collections and relationships for agents
Passport lets callers use APIs without holding the secret and logs every call
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page
Passport access requires admin approval of scope for each request
